stats.label: Expected response time for 88% of customers

blocks.text: Setting up Gmail on your Mac for support workflows

Google does not offer a standalone Gmail app for macOS. Most support leads prefer creating a dedicated web app. Open Gmail in Safari or Chrome. In Safari, go to File > Add to Dock. This creates a separate icon in your Dock. It acts like a native app. You get better focus and fewer distractions from other browser tabs.
Essential keyboard shortcuts for support leads

Speed is critical when you handle dozens of tickets per hour. Go to Settings > General > Keyboard shortcuts to enable them. Once active, press ? to see the full list. Use c to compose, e to archive, and r to reply. These small habits save minutes every hour. Over a week, this adds up to significant time saved.
Managing high volume email with labels and filters

Support leads must categorize incoming mail immediately. Use filters to sort emails by sender or subject. Go to Settings > Filters and Blocked Addresses. Create a filter to automatically move tickets from specific clients into dedicated labels. This keeps your primary inbox clean and ensures urgent escalations remain visible.
If you struggle to find a specific setting, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur where it is. It will circle the button on your screen so you can find it without searching through menus.
blocks.title: Find buttons faster

blocks.text: Typing long explanations for complex support issues is exhausting. Use dictation to draft your replies. Hold the fn key to start speaking. Speak clearly to ensure the text is formatted correctly. This is useful for building internal knowledge base articles or explaining steps to a customer.
Handling email limits and system errors

Personal Gmail accounts have a limit of 500 recipients per day. Workspace accounts allow up to 2,000. If you hit these limits, Gmail blocks your account for 24 hours. Monitor your volume if you send mass updates to customers. If you see a 502 error, refresh the page or clear your browser cache.

faq.question: Is there an official Gmail app for Mac?
faq.answer: No. Google does not provide a native desktop application for macOS. Users typically create a web app through Safari or Chrome to simulate a standalone experience.

faq.question: How do I speed up my Gmail workflow?
faq.answer: Enable keyboard shortcuts in Settings. Use keys like c to compose and e to archive. This reduces your reliance on the mouse and keeps your hands on the keyboard.

faq.question: What should I do if my Gmail is slow?
faq.answer: Check your browser extensions for conflicts. Ensure your macOS is updated to the latest version. If the issue persists, try accessing your mail in a private window to rule out cache problems.
